findings.title: SendGrid client API key is not initialized in scheduleEmailReminders
findings.body: `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` imports `client` from `@sendgrid/client` and calls `client.request(...)` on lines 57 and 188, but never calls `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` (only `sgMail.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` is called on line 19). Unless `emailReminderManager.ts` happens to have been imported in the same serverless instance beforehand, `@sendgrid/client` has no API key set and both cancelling scheduled sends (`/v3/user/scheduled_sends`) and creating batch IDs (`/v3/mail/batch`) will fail with 401 Unauthorized.

findings.title: Rescheduling a booking immediately cancels in SendGrid and deletes the booking before reminders are cleaned up
findings.body:
In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` is called with `immediateDelete = true` (line 968) and without `await`, right before `eventManager.reschedule(...)` (line 978). There are two issues here:
1. Passing `immediateDelete = true` sends a `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends` immediately to SendGrid even when the reminder is days away, re-introducing the 100 pending cancellations limit that this PR is meant to avoid, and `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` does not delete the `WorkflowReminder` row in the `immediateDelete` branch.
2. `eventManager.reschedule` deletes the `originalRescheduledBooking` row in the database, and because `WorkflowReminder.booking` has `onDelete: Cascade`, any un-awaited `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` calls race with the cascade delete (and if changed to `immediateDelete = false`, the cascade delete would wipe out the `WorkflowReminder` row before the cron job in `scheduleEmailReminders` ever sees `cancelled: true`, leaving the scheduled email active in SendGrid).

findings.title: A single SendGrid error in the cancellation loop aborts all deletions in the batch
findings.body: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` (lines 53-77), `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` promises are collected in `workflowRemindersToDelete` and only executed at `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` after the loop finishes (Prisma queries are lazy until awaited). If `client.request` throws for the Nth reminder (for example, if its `referenceId` is missing or rejected by SendGrid), the `catch` block is entered before `Promise.all` runs, so none of the prior N-1 reminders that were already cancelled in SendGrid get deleted from the database and they will be retried on every cron run.

findings.title: Un-awaited reminder cancellations race with cascade deletion of workflow and workflowStep
findings.body: In `workflowsRouter.delete` (lines 212-225) and `workflowsRouter.update` when a step is deleted (lines 519-531), `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are called inside `.forEach(...)` without `await`, immediately followed by `await ctx.prisma.workflow.deleteMany(...)` or `await ctx.prisma.workflowStep.delete(...)`. Because `WorkflowStep` and `WorkflowReminder` have `onDelete: Cascade`, the database cascade deletes the `WorkflowReminder` rows while `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` (when `referenceId` is null) and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are concurrently trying to `prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminder.id } })`, causing P2025 record-not-found errors and risking unfinished external API calls if the serverless function terminates after the mutation returns.
